1	# US-04 HC3 round 1: the human's feedback and the decisions (2026-11-22)
2	
3	The human ran the HC3 QA on the local stack (branch `feat/us-04-design-system`, not pushed) and asked
4	for changes. Verbatim (Spanish), with the four screenshots they attached described in brackets:
5	
6	> "[calendar screenshot: on a wide screen the calendar popover opens ABOVE the date field, covering the
7	> header and the fields above it; it is very large, day cells ~80 px] mira como se ve el calendario,
8	> deberia desplegarlo ahi abajo, [screenshot: typed '29/20/2001' in Fecha de nacimiento, the error
9	> shown is 'Ingresa tu fecha de nacimiento.'] si escribo la fecha mira que no me deja. y valida los
10	> inputs si son de type text, number, etcc, porque en nombre me deja escribir numero y con un maximo de
11	> caractes en cada input como lo recomiendes. El fondo si puedes hacerlo un poco mas claro y con
12	> degradado quedaria bien. [screenshot: step 1 header and step indicator] tambien agregarle flechas para
13	> regresar a un modulo anterior o si quiere cambiar quizas de colombia a chile. [screenshot: the
14	> country chooser: only 'Elige tu país' and two cards on a dark empty page, no header] esta muy simple
15	> visualmente, puedes agregarle como un texto de más un header, y lo mismo del bg para todas. Dejalo
16	> corriendo en local para ver los cambios, el tiempo para que lo resuelvas es crucial pero hazlo bien"
17	
18	Translation: the calendar should drop down below the field; typing the date "won't let me"; validate the
19	inputs by type (text, number, etc.) because the name accepts digits, and a maximum length on every input
20	as you recommend; make the background a bit lighter with a gradient; add arrows to go back to the
21	previous step or to change country (e.g. Colombia to Chile); the country chooser is visually too simple:
22	add some text and a header, and the same background on every page.
23	
24	This is an explicit human instruction (CLAUDE.md §1). It overrides the US-04 rule "logic does not
25	change" for the points below only, and it adds to the CLAUDE.md §5 frontend-design override "no extra
26	sections the spec does not ask for": the human now asks for them on the chooser. The concrete values
27	below are the main session's recommendation ("como lo recomiendes"); the human reviews them in the HC3
28	QA of this round.
29	
30	## D1. Calendar placement and size (wide screens)
31	- From `--breakpoint-sheet` up, the calendar is an anchored popover **directly below the date input**,
32	  start-aligned with it. It never opens above the field when it can fit below: before opening, if the
33	  space below the field is smaller than the popover, the page scrolls so the field sits near the top of
34	  the viewport (below the sticky header) and the popover fits below. Opening above stays only as the
35	  last fallback (viewport shorter than field + popover).
36	- The popover is **compact**: max width about 22rem; day cells 44×44 CSS px (the touch-target minimum,
37	  not larger); header (month and year + "Elegir año" + prev/next) and "Cerrar" sized to match. Target
38	  total height ≤ about 26rem. It must not cover the sticky wizard header.
39	- Narrow screens keep the bottom sheet (unchanged).
40	- Keyboard, focus trap, focus return and ARIA unchanged (US-04-AC-09).
41	
42	## D2. Typed date: input mask and a clear error
43	- The date text box accepts **digits only** as typed; the `/` separators are **inserted automatically**
44	  after the day and the month (typing `15051990` shows `15/05/1990`); backspace works naturally over a
45	  separator; `maxlength` 10; `inputmode="numeric"`; placeholder `dd/mm/aaaa` kept. A pasted
46	  `15/05/1990`, `15-05-1990`, `15.05.1990` or `15051990` ends as `15/05/1990`.
47	- Typing a **valid** date (for example `15/05/1990`) is accepted and stored as ISO `1990-05-15`, the
48	  same as choosing it in the calendar (verify this works end to end; the human reported "no me deja").
49	- When the text is complete but **not a real date** (`29/20/2001`, `31/02/1990`) or **incomplete** when
50	  the person leaves the field, the error shown is a code-owned message
51	  **"Fecha no válida. Usa el formato dd/mm/aaaa."**, not the Strapi `requiredMessage`
52	  ("Ingresa tu fecha de nacimiento.", which stays for an empty field) and not the minAge message.
53	  A real date under 18 years keeps the Strapi minAge `errorMessage`. Error timing unchanged (touched or
54	  submit attempt).
55	- The stored model stays ISO or `''` (no contract change).
56	
57	## D3. Input profiles: allowed characters, max length, keyboard hints
58	A front-end presentation/behaviour map by field key, like the icon map (`field-icons.ts`), with a
59	default for unknown keys (no filter). Characters outside the profile are dropped as they are typed or
60	pasted (the caret stays where it was); validation rules from Strapi stay the source of truth.
61	- `maxlength` attribute on every text/number field = the Strapi `maxLength` rule value when present
62	  (generic, works for new fields from Strapi). Fallback when a field has no `maxLength` rule: the
63	  profile's max, if any.
64	- Profiles:
65	  - `fullName`: letters (any Unicode letter, so á é í ó ú ü ñ), space, apostrophe `'`, hyphen `-`,
66	    period `.`; no digits; `autocomplete="name"`, `autocapitalize="words"`; max 80.
67	  - `documentNumber`: digits only; but when the field has a `rutCheckDigit` rule (the Chilean RUT)
68	    digits, `.`, `-`, `k`, `K` (k shown uppercase); `inputmode="numeric"` for the digits-only
69	    variant, `inputmode="text"` for RUT; max 10 (digits only) / 12 (RUT) via Strapi `maxLength`.
70	  - `plate`: letters and digits only, shown uppercase (the stored value uppercase too is acceptable
71	    only if validation already accepts it; the patterns are case-insensitive, so yes); max 6;
72	    `autocapitalize="characters"`, `autocomplete="off"`.
73	  - `model`: letters, digits, space, `-`, `.`, `/`; max 40.
74	  - `vehicleYear` (type number) and any `number` field: digits only, no `e`, `+`, `-`, `.`, `,`;
75	    max 4 for vehicleYear; `inputmode="numeric"`. (If the number field is a native
76	    `type="number"`, switch it to `type="text"` + `inputmode="numeric"` so `maxlength` and the filter
77	    work; the model keeps the string per ADR-0004.)
78	- Strapi seed content (no schema change, contract unchanged):
79	  - `fullName` (CO and CL) gets a `pattern` rule `^[\p{L}][\p{L} '.-]*$`-equivalent that the existing
80	    validator can evaluate (check how `pattern` rules are compiled; if the `u` flag is not used, write
81	    the class explicitly: `^[A-Za-zÁÉÍÓÚÜÑáéíóúüñ][A-Za-zÁÉÍÓÚÜÑáéíóúüñ '.-]*$`) so pasted digits are
82	    still rejected; its `errorMessage` becomes
83	    "Ingresa tu nombre completo, solo letras (entre 3 y 80 caracteres)."
84	  - `documentNumber` CO gets `maxLength` 10; CL (RUT) gets `maxLength` 12.
85	  - `plate` CO and CL get `maxLength` 6.
86	  - Follow the existing seed rule for already-seeded databases (do not change it); the local demo is
87	    reset with `docker compose -p mci-demo down -v`.
88

25	## 1. Summary
26	
27	A visual redesign of the whole quoting wizard (country chooser, step 1 form, plan list, summary,
28	payment and confirmation) on a tokenized design system, for people in Colombia and Chile on
29	phone, tablet and desktop. It adds country flags and a per-country accent, icons, an accessible
30	custom select and date picker (replacing the browser's native ones), a step indicator, step
31	transitions, skeletons and micro-animations that all honour `prefers-reduced-motion`, a
32	mobile-first responsive layout with 44 × 44 px targets, and self-hosted typography. Behaviour,
33	validation, stored values, routes and the Strapi contracts do not change; the existing tests keep
34	passing with the same strength, adapted only where a native element is replaced (§11.1).
35

80	## 3. Glossary
81	
82	Terms of the US-01..US-03 glossaries keep their meaning.
83	
84	| Term | Meaning in this project |
85	|---|---|
86	| Token | A CSS custom property declared in the single token file (BR-01). |
87	| Primitive / semantic / component token | Raw values (`--primitive-violet-400`), roles (`--color-text-muted`, `--space-4`), and per-component bindings (`--component-button-primary-bg`). Prefixes per ADR-0010 §1. Components use semantic or component tokens only. |
88	| Loose value | A literal colour, length, font, shadow, gradient, duration, easing or z-index in a component style instead of a `var(--…)` (allowed literals in BR-01). |
89	| Country accent | The per-country accent colour token, set from the current country context (BR-03). |
90	| Custom select | The design-system replacement for a `select` field: a WAI-ARIA combobox with a listbox popup (BR-05). A **select-only** custom select (fewer than 4 options) has a `<button>` as its combobox element; a **searchable** one has an `<input>` (ADR-0012 §3). |
91	| Searchable select | A custom select whose option count reaches the search threshold; typing filters the options (US-04-Q-11). |
92	| Date field | The design-system replacement for a `date` field: a text box for typed entry plus an "Elegir fecha" button that opens the calendar (BR-06). |
93	| Calendar | The WAI-ARIA date picker dialog opened from the date field. |
94	| Shown value | What a control displays: the option label of a custom select, the dd/mm/aaaa text of a date field. An empty select-only custom select shows the prompt "Selecciona una opción" as its button text; an empty searchable one shows the prompt as its placeholder, and its input value (`inputValue()`) is `''`. |
95	| Stored value | The value in the editing model and in the `quote-wizard` entry (ADR-0003, ADR-0004): option `value`, ISO `YYYY-MM-DD`, or `''`. Unchanged by US-04. |
96	| Panel | The popup of a custom select or the calendar: an anchored popover on wide screens, a bottom sheet below `--breakpoint-sheet` (37.5em, 600 CSS px; US-04-Q-13, ADR-0010 §6). |
97	| Wizard header | New top bar on the wizard pages with the product name and the country chip (flag + country name). |
98	| Step indicator | New progress display of the three wizard steps (US-04-Q-17). |

# MCP Server Instructions

The following MCP servers have provided instructions for how to use their tools and resources:

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>\n\n<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>\n\n<?claude block s1?>\n\n<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

778	## 9. Non-functional requirements
779	
780	- **Accessibility:** WCAG 2.2 AA; WAI-ARIA APG combobox (select-only and list autocomplete) and
781	  date picker dialog patterns; visible focus on the focused element; Tab order unchanged except the
782	  "Elegir fecha" stop; one `h1` per page; decorative icons and flags hidden; `forced-colors`
783	  fallbacks for gradient text and borders; screen reader pass at HC3 (NVDA or VoiceOver) on the
784	  select (both kinds, including how a collapsed combobox without `aria-controls` is announced,
785	  ADR-0012), the calendar, the year list and the step indicator.
786	- **Responsive:** mobile-first CSS (`min-width` queries on the `--breakpoint-*` tokens); 320–1440
787	  CSS px with no horizontal scroll (verified at 360, 768, 1280); 44 × 44 px targets; bottom sheet
788	  below `--breakpoint-sheet` (600 px), fitting above the on-screen keyboard on phones (HC3 phone
789	  check, AC-12).
790	- **Multi-country:** one build; no country branch except the presentation map
791	  `country-visuals.ts` (ADR-0011, enforced by the static guard of AC-03); calendar names, date
792	  formatting and the first day of the week from `Intl`/CLDR and the country `localeTag`, with no
793	  country code in the date picker; the date text format is the same for every country.
794	- **Security / privacy:** no third-party origin at runtime (fonts, icons, flags self-hosted, so no
795	  new CSP or proxy change); no value of the form in logs; no `innerHTML` for icons or flags (the
796	  existing static guard applies: icons and flags are components or inline template SVG).
797	- **Performance:** icons imported individually; fonts: one latin-subset variable WOFF2 file per
798	  family with the weight range limited to the scale (BR-12), text face preloaded; the step 1 page is
799	  lazy-loaded (`loadComponent`, ADR-0012 §7) so `@angular/aria`, `@angular/cdk` and the step 1
800	  icons stay out of the initial bundle; the production build stays within the existing
801	  `angular.json` budgets (initial 500 kB warning, 1 MB error; component styles 4 kB warning, 8 kB
802	  error), which are not changed. Movement animates `transform` and `opacity` only; state
803	  transitions may change paint-only properties (colours, border colour, shadow); no layout
804	  property is animated (ADR-0013).
805	- **Maintainability:** tokens in one file; new shared components and pure functions under
806	  `src/app/shared/` with the names of ADR-0012 §2 (`CustomSelect`, `DateField`, `Calendar`,
807	  `date-text.ts`, `calendar-dates.ts`, `select-search.ts`), ADR-0010 (`field-icons.ts`, flag
808	  components under `shared/flags/`) and ADR-0011 (`country-visuals.ts`); others per CLAUDE.md §6
809	  (for example `step-indicator.ts` → `StepIndicator`).
810	- **Language:** end-user copy Spanish; code, docs English.

into it: the bottom sheet sits above the on-screen keyboard, and the search input, the active

its own search box, a dialog) changes the ARIA pattern on narrow screens and needs a spec change
first (ADR-0012 *Spec impact* 5).

### US-04-AC-13 — Step indicator and wizard header (derived from US-04-BR-09, BR-08 / Q-17)

```gherkin
Scenario Outline: Step indicator and wizard header
  Given I am on <page> in Colombia
  Then the step indicator lists "Tus datos", "Plan", "Resumen y pago" in this order
  And <current> has aria-current="step" and the text "Paso <n> de 3" is available to assistive technology
  And steps before it are marked "completado"
  And neither the indicator nor the header contains a focusable element or a heading

  Examples:
    | page          | current          | n |
    | "/co/datos"   | "Tus datos"      | 1 |
    | "/co/planes"  | "Plan"           | 2 |
    | "/co/resumen" | "Resumen y pago" | 3 |

Scenario: Indicator on the confirmation
  When the payment is confirmed
  Then all three steps are marked "completado" and none has aria-current
```

### US-04-AC-14 — Step transition keeps focus and one page (derived from US-04-BR-09 / Q-14)

```gherkin
Scenario: Step transition keeps focus and one page
  Given motion is allowed and I completed step 1 in Colombia
  When I activate "Continuar"
  Then at no moment during the transition does the document contain more than one h1 or more than one main
  And the focus ends on the h1 "Elige tu plan" and the document title is "Elige tu plan | Cotizador de seguro de auto"
  And the transition lasts at most the "slow" duration token
```

The transition is enter-only (`animate.enter` on the arriving page, no `animate.leave`), so the
leaving page is removed at once (ADR-0013 §2). The "slow" token is `--duration-slow` (320 ms); the
page enter uses `--duration-base` (200 ms). A `MutationObserver` installed before "Continuar"
records the maximum `h1` and `main` counts (ADR-0013 §4).

### US-04-AC-15 — Skeletons while content loads (derived from US-04-BR-09 / Q-15)

```gherkin
Scenario Outline: Skeletons while content loads
  Given the content backend has not answered the <request> request yet
  When <place> is shown
  Then skeleton shapes are shown, hidden from assistive technology
  And the text "<loading text>" is still in the polite live region
  When the content arrives
  Then the skeleton is replaced by the content

  Examples:
    | request     | place                  | loading text |
    | form fields | step 1 in Colombia     | Cargando formulario… |
    | plans       | step 2 in Colombia     | Cargando planes… |
    | terms       | the summary terms      | Cargando términos y condiciones… |
    | countries   | the country chooser    | Cargando… |
```

### US-04-AC-16 — Interactive plan cards (derived from US-04-BR-09)

```gherkin
Scenario: Interactive plan cards
  Given step 2 is shown in Chile
  When I click the short description of "Plan Premium"
  Then the radio "Plan Premium" is checked and no other plan is
  And "Plan Protegido" keeps the "Recomendado" badge and the recommended style
  And each coverage and benefit item shows a check-circle icon hidden from assistive technology
  When I use the arrow keys in the plan group
  Then the choice follows the native radio behaviour of US-02-AC-16, unchanged
```

### US-04-AC-17 — Reduced motion (derived from US-04-BR-10)

```gherkin
Scenario: Reduced motion
  Given the browser reports prefers-reduced-motion: reduce
  When I go through step 1 (opening "Ciudad" and the calendar), step 2, the summary and the confirmation in Colombia
  Then at every page and with every panel open, every element's computed animation-duration and transition-duration are 0s
  And document.getAnimations() returns an empty list

Scenario: Reduced motion by construction
  Given the production style files and sources of frontend/src
  Then outside tokens.css every animation and transition declaration is inside a @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) block
  And tokens.css sets every --duration-* and --delay-* token to 0ms under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce
  And every CDK overlay and dialog is created with disableAnimations: true
```

The second scenario is the static guard of ADR-0013 §4. `disableAnimations` matters because the
CDK backdrop otherwise keeps a 1 ms transition under reduced motion (ADR-0013 §3).

```gherkin

    step 1 after a failed "Continuar", step 2, the summary and the confirmation

    | 1280  | 800    | Chile    | in at least two columns |
```

### US-04-AC-19 — Fonts and assets are local (derived from US-04-BR-12 / Q-08)

```gherkin
Scenario: Fonts and assets are local
  When I go through the whole flow in Colombia
```

With variable fonts each family is one file covering a weight range (BR-12, ADR-0010 §5); the
static guard counts `@font-face` families, and the e2e counts font requests.

## 9. Non-functional requirements

- **Accessibility:** WCAG 2.2 AA; WAI-ARIA APG combobox (select-only and list autocomplete) and
  date picker dialog patterns; visible focus on the focused element; Tab order unchanged except the
  "Elegir fecha" stop; one `h1` per page; decorative icons and flags hidden; `forced-colors`
  fallbacks for gradient text and borders; screen reader pass at HC3 (NVDA or VoiceOver) on the
  select (both kinds, including how a collapsed combobox without `aria-controls` is announced,
  ADR-0012), the calendar, the year list and the step indicator.
- **Responsive:** mobile-first CSS (`min-width` queries on the `--breakpoint-*` tokens); 320–1440
  CSS px with no horizontal scroll (verified at 360, 768, 1280); 44 × 44 px targets; bottom sheet
  below `--breakpoint-sheet` (600 px), fitting above the on-screen keyboard on phones (HC3 phone
  check, AC-12).
- **Multi-country:** one build; no country branch except the presentation map
  `country-visuals.ts` (ADR-0011, enforced by the static guard of AC-03); calendar names, date
  formatting and the first day of the week from `Intl`/CLDR and the country `localeTag`, with no
  country code in the date picker; the date text format is the same for every country.
- **Security / privacy:** no third-party origin at runtime (fonts, icons, flags self-hosted, so no
  new CSP or proxy change); no value of the form in logs; no `innerHTML` for icons or flags (the
  existing static guard applies: icons and flags are components or inline template SVG).
- **Performance:** icons imported individually; fonts: one latin-subset variable WOFF2 file per
  family with the weight range limited to the scale (BR-12), text face preloaded; the step 1 page is
  lazy-loaded (`loadComponent`, ADR-0012 §7) so `@angular/aria`, `@angular/cdk` and the step 1
  icons stay out of the initial bundle; the production build stays within the existing
  `angular.json` budgets (initial 500 kB warning, 1 MB error; component styles 4 kB warning, 8 kB
  error), which are not changed. Movement animates `transform` and `opacity` only; state
  transitions may change paint-only properties (colours, border colour, shadow); no layout
  property is animated (ADR-0013).
- **Maintainability:** tokens in one file; new shared components and pure functions under
  `src/app/shared/` with the names of ADR-0012 §2 (`CustomSelect`, `DateField`, `Calendar`,
  `date-text.ts`, `calendar-dates.ts`, `select-search.ts`), ADR-0010 (`field-icons.ts`, flag
  components under `shared/flags/`) and ADR-0011 (`country-visuals.ts`); others per CLAUDE.md §6
  (for example `step-indicator.ts` → `StepIndicator`).
- **Language:** end-user copy Spanish; code, docs English.

lines: | US-04-BR-04 | "Icons: a single library with SVG icons imported individually … inside the inputs (document, name, date, city, plate, make, model, year), in the wizard steps, in the plans, in help, error and success messages. The input icon comes from a front-end mapping by field key, with a generic default icon for new fields … Decorative icons `aria-hidden`; icons that carry meaning have a label." | One icon library, icons imported one by one (no full-set import, no icon font, no runtime fetch): `@lucide/angular` 1.77.0, ISC (US-04-Q-09, ADR-0010 §7). Step 1: every `text`, `number`, `select` and `date` field shows the icon mapped from its `key` (§7.2), or the default icon for any other key; `checkbox` fields show none. Icons in steps, plan lists (check-circle), help, error and success messages. Every icon that sits next to text saying the same thing is decorative: `aria-hidden="true"`, not focusable, no `<title>` and no text content, so no accessible name or `textContent` of a control changes. An icon without adjacent text (an icon-only button) has an accessible name from §8.1. | US-04-AC-04, US-04-AC-20 |

| US-04-BR-05 | "Select: our own dropdown in the design system's style, with an icon, search when the list is long (e.g. cities, makes), and the selected option marked." "Built on accessible primitives, not from scratch … Full accessibility per the WAI-ARIA patterns (combobox/listbox …): arrows, Enter, Escape, Home/End … screen-reader announcements." | Every `select` field renders a custom select following the WAI-ARIA combobox pattern with a listbox popup (select-only below the search threshold, editable with list filtering at or above it, US-04-Q-11). The element that takes focus is the element the field's `<label for>` points at (a `<button>` for a select-only, an `<input type="text">` for a searchable select, ADR-0012 §3, so `label.control`, `getByLabel` and `labels[0]` keep working) and carries `role="combobox"`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-required`, `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby` as the native control did, plus `aria-controls` referring to the listbox **while the list is rendered** (`@angular/aria` omits it while collapsed, at least before the first open; ADR-0012 *Consequences*; checked with a screen reader at HC3). Empty, the prompt "Selecciona una opción" is its shown value: the button's text for a select-only, the placeholder for a searchable select (whose input value is then `''`). The prompt is not an option (supersedes the "first entry is a non-selectable prompt" wording of US-01-BR-02, US-04-Q-04). The listbox contains exactly the configured options in `sortOrder`; the selected option is marked visually (check icon + style) and with `aria-selected="true"`. Choosing an option stores its `value` (unchanged). Keyboard per US-04-AC-06; built on `@angular/aria` 22.3.0 and `@angular/cdk` 22.3.0 (US-04-Q-04, ADR-0012). | US-04-AC-05, US-04-AC-06, US-04-AC-07, US-04-AC-12 |

| US-04-BR-06 | "Calendar (birth date): our own date picker with month navigation and fast year navigation (a year selector …), days disabled according to the rules (minAge), and the date can also be typed by hand." Same accessibility clause as BR-05: "date picker dialog … focus trapped and returned on close". | Every `date` field renders a text box (the labelled control) and an "Elegir fecha" button that opens the calendar (WAI-ARIA date picker dialog). Typed entry: format dd/mm/aaaa for every country, independent of the browser locale, parsed and stored as ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` (US-04-Q-05). Text that is not a complete, existing date is treated exactly like the former `validity.badInput` (US-01-BR-01, US-01-AC-09 note): stored `''`, text kept visible, field invalid whether required or optional, same message resolution. Calendar: month navigation, year selector, keyboard per US-04-AC-09, a CDK modal dialog (ADR-0012 §4) with focus trapped while open, a backdrop, the page behind hidden from assistive technology (`aria-hidden="true"`), and focus returned to "Elegir fecha" on close. The first day of the week (grid column order and the week bounds of Home/End) follows the country's locale (`localeTag`) from CLDR week data: Sunday for es-CO, Monday for es-CL. It is derived from the locale at runtime, with no country code or per-country table in the date picker (human decision at HC1, 2026-11-21). A day is disabled if and only if the shared validator of the field (the same pure function used for validation, no second implementation) rejects that date for a reason other than "required" (with the seed's `minAge` 18: every day after the 18th anniversary limit and every future day). Disabled days can still be typed; typing one shows the configured message (validation unchanged). **v0.3 (HC3):** the typed entry gets a mask and text that is not a complete, existing date shows the code-owned message "Fecha no válida. Usa el formato dd/mm/aaaa." instead of the former `badInput` message resolution (BR-18 supersedes the "same message resolution" clause above; stored `''` unchanged). On wide screens the calendar is a compact popover directly below the date text box (BR-17). | US-04-AC-08, US-04-AC-09, US-04-AC-10, US-04-AC-12, US-04-AC-24, US-04-AC-25 |

| US-04-BR-08 | "Supporting text: clear microcopy in help texts, placeholders, empty states and errors … Business content keeps coming from Strapi; only interface texts live in the front end." | Front-end copy added by US-04 is exactly §8.1 (Spanish, same for both countries). Existing code-owned strings (US-01..US-03 §8.1) and every Strapi text stay unchanged (US-04-Q-07). Day and month names come from `Intl` with the country's `localeTag`, not from literals. | US-04-AC-07, US-04-AC-09, US-04-AC-11, US-04-AC-13 |

| US-04-BR-09 | "Interactions and animation: an animated wizard step indicator, transition between steps, hover/focus/active/disabled states, validation with soft feedback, skeletons while Strapi loads, plan selection with interactive cards, and a summary with micro-animations." | Step indicator per US-04-Q-17 (not focusable, current step exposed with `aria-current="step"`). Step change: enter-only transition of the arriving page (no two pages in the DOM at once), focus on the arriving `h1` as today (US-04-Q-14). Every interactive control has distinct hover, focus-visible, active and disabled (including `aria-disabled`) styles. Soft feedback: an error appears with a short fade and its icon, no shaking, no colour-only signal. Skeletons replace the loading text visually on step 1, step 2, the terms region and the country list, while the existing loading text stays in its live region (US-04-Q-15). Plan cards: a pointer click anywhere on a card chooses its plan; the native radio stays the keyboard and accessibility control. Summary and confirmation micro-animations per US-04-Q-16. Mechanism: Angular native `animate.enter` and CSS on the duration and easing tokens, no animation library, no `animate.leave` on pages (ADR-0013). Movement uses `transform` and `opacity` only; state changes may transition paint-only properties (colours, border colour, shadow); the 2 px card lift on hover applies only under `(hover: hover)`. | US-04-AC-13, US-04-AC-14, US-04-AC-15, US-04-AC-16, US-04-AC-23 |

| US-04-BR-10 | "Everything honors `prefers-reduced-motion`: no movement if the user asks for it." | With `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, every CSS animation and transition and every Angular enter/leave animation has a computed duration of 0 s (or none), `document.getAnimations()` is empty, and no element changes position, size or rotation over time (skeleton shimmer, step transition, panel slide, indicator fill, spinner, micro-animations all off). States still change instantly. By construction (ADR-0013 §3): outside `tokens.css` every `animation*`/`transition*` declaration sits inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`; `tokens.css` sets every `--duration-*` and `--delay-*` to `0ms` under `reduce`; every CDK overlay and dialog is created with `disableAnimations: true`. A static guard checks the three. | US-04-AC-17 |

| US-04-BR-11 | "Responsive, mobile-first: … at least 360×740, 768×1024 and 1280×800, with no horizontal scroll, touch targets of at least 44×44 px, and a layout that reorganizes (for example, plans in a column on mobile and in a grid on desktop)." | At each of the three viewports, on every page and with a select panel or the calendar open: `document.documentElement.scrollWidth ≤ window.innerWidth`; every interactive element (link, button, combobox, text box, option, calendar day, and for a native checkbox or radio the box of the input together with its `<label>`) has a hit box of at least 44 × 44 CSS px. Styles are written mobile-first (base styles for the narrowest width, `min-width` queries upward). Plans: one column at 360 px, at least two columns at 1280 px. This raises the 24 × 24 px of US-01-AC-26, US-02-AC-18 and US-03-AC-18 to 44 × 44 (US-04-Q-18). On a phone, a searchable select's bottom sheet fits above the on-screen keyboard: the search input, the active option and at least one option row stay visible while the keyboard is up (manual HC3 phone check, AC-12 note; ADR-0012 *Spec impact* 5). | US-04-AC-12, US-04-AC-18 |

| US-04-BR-12 | "Typography: at most 2 families, loaded efficiently." | At most two `@font-face` families (Archivo and Atkinson Hyperlegible Next, ADR-0010 §5, US-04-Q-08). Each family is **one variable WOFF2 file** (latin subset), self-hosted on the app origin (`/fonts/…`), `font-display: swap`; "at most the weights the type scale uses" means each `@font-face` `font-weight` descriptor is limited to the range the scale uses (Archivo `700 800`, Atkinson Hyperlegible Next `400 700`), not one file per weight. `font-family` declarations name at most those two families plus a system fallback stack (`system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif`) of **local** fonts that are never downloaded; the fallback names are not counted as families. No request to a third-party origin at runtime for fonts, icons, flags or styles. | US-04-AC-19 |

The Tab order of every page is the one of US-01-AC-24, US-02-AC-16 and US-03-AC-16, plus only the "Elegir fecha" button after each date text box; the wizard header and the step indicator add no Tab stop. Each page keeps exactly one `h1` (the step heading), the existing `h2`/`h3` levels and the ADR-0009 terms levels; visual size comes from tokens and never changes a heading level; header, indicator, panels and calendar add no heading element. | US-04-AC-06, US-04-AC-09, US-04-AC-20 |

| US-04-BR-14 | "Exact versions of any new dependency, license reviewed." | Every new dependency is added with `npm install -E`, has an exact version in `frontend/package.json`, is listed in the relevant ADR with its version, license and justification, and its license is permissive (MIT, ISC, Apache-2.0, BSD, OFL-1.1 for fonts) unless the human accepts another. Accepted additions: `@lucide/angular` 1.77.0 (ISC), `@fontsource-variable/archivo` 5.3.0 (OFL-1.1), `@fontsource-variable/atkinson-hyperlegible-next` 5.3.0 (OFL-1.1) (ADR-0010); `@angular/cdk` 22.3.0 (MIT), `@angular/aria` 22.3.0 (MIT) (ADR-0012). No animation library (ADR-0013). | US-04-AC-21 |

| US-04-BR-17 | (HC3 round 1, human, 2026-11-22) "mira como se ve el calendario, deberia desplegarlo ahi abajo" (screenshot: on a wide screen the calendar opens above the field, covers the header, day cells ~80 px). | From `--breakpoint-sheet` (600 CSS px) up, the calendar dialog is a popover **directly below the date text box**: its top edge is 0–16 CSS px below the text box's bottom edge and its left edge within 8 CSS px of the text box's left edge (shifted left only as far as needed to stay inside the viewport). Before it opens, if the space between the text box's bottom and the viewport bottom is smaller than the popover's height, the page scrolls so that the date field sits just below the sticky wizard header, and the popover then opens below it. It opens **above** only as the last fallback, when the viewport height minus the header height is smaller than the text box height plus the popover height. The popover never overlaps the sticky wizard header and lies entirely inside the viewport. **Compact:** width ≤ 22rem (352 CSS px); day cells 44–48 CSS px wide and tall (the 44 × 44 minimum of BR-11, not larger); month/year header, "Elegir año", "Mes anterior", "Mes siguiente" and "Cerrar" sized to match (each ≥ 44 × 44); total height target ≤ 26rem (416 CSS px), limit 28rem (448 CSS px), with six week rows shown. Below `--breakpoint-sheet` the bottom sheet of AC-12 is unchanged. Modal dialog, keyboard, focus trap, focus return and ARIA are unchanged (AC-09). Mechanism per ADR-0014. | US-04-AC-24 |
| US-04-BR-18 | (HC3 round 1) "si escribo la fecha mira que no me deja" (screenshot: "29/20/2001" typed, message "Ingresa tu fecha de nacimiento."). | **Mask.** The date text box accepts digits as typed; any other typed character is dropped, except a separator (`/`, `-`, `.`): typed after a one-digit day or month it pads that group with a leading zero and shows `/` ("5/" → "05/"); typed right after a complete two-digit day or month it shows `/` once; anywhere else it is dropped. A `/` is inserted automatically between the day and the month and between the month and the year as soon as the next digit is typed ("150" → "15/0"; `15051990` → "15/05/1990"). At most 8 digits (`maxlength` 10). Backspace removes the character before the caret; a separator left with no digit after it goes with the digit before it ("15/05/1990" + End + 4 × Backspace → "15/05"). `inputmode="numeric"`; placeholder "dd/mm/aaaa" and hint kept. **Paste:** text that the existing typed-date parser accepts (US-04-Q-05: `d/m/yyyy` with `/`, `-` or `.`, or `ddmmyyyy`) is shown as dd/mm/aaaa ("15.05.1990" → "15/05/1990", "5/5/1990" → "05/05/1990"); other pasted text goes through the mask digit by digit. **Stored value** unchanged: ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` for a complete, existing date, else `''` (ADR-0003, ADR-0004). A complete valid date typed by hand is accepted and stored exactly as the same date chosen in the calendar. **Message.** On a field whose text is not empty but is not a complete, existing date (incomplete, such as "15/05/199" or "15/05"; impossible, such as "29/20/2001", "31/02/1990", "29/02/2001"), the error is the code-owned "Fecha no válida. Usa el formato dd/mm/aaaa.", for required **and** optional date fields (US-04-Q-24), replacing the former `badInput` message resolution (US-01-AC-09 note) for dates. An empty required field keeps `requiredMessage` ?? `errorMessage` ("Ingresa tu fecha de nacimiento."); a real date that fails a rule keeps the rule's message ("Debes ser mayor de edad (18 años o más) para cotizar."). Error timing (after leaving the field or a submit attempt) and focus on a failed "Continuar" unchanged. | US-04-AC-25, US-04-AC-08 |
| US-04-BR-19 | (HC3 round 1) "valida los inputs si son de type text, number, etcc, porque en nombre me deja escribir numero y con un maximo de caractes en cada input como lo recomiendes". | Each `text` and `number` field of step 1 takes an **input profile** from the front-end map of §7.2, by field `key`; an unmapped `number` field takes the "digits" profile; any other unmapped field has no character filter. Characters outside the profile are dropped as they are typed or pasted; the rest of the text is kept and the caret stays after the last kept character of the edit. Letter case is applied as typed where the profile says so (plate: upper case, shown and stored). lines: | US-04-Q-04 | **[Blocks HC1] [ADR]** Custom select and date picker: which accessible primitives (Angular CDK Overlay/Listbox/A11y vs `@angular/aria` at 22.3.0), and how they bind to Signal Forms and the shared validation core (ADR-0004) without changing validation or stored values. The test changes of §11.1 depend on the element chosen. | Decided by an ADR (§10). Constraints the spec sets: the focusable element is labelable (`<input>` or `<button>`) and targeted by the field's `<label for>`; it is the control `focusBoundControl()` focuses; the model keeps strings (option value, ISO date, `''`); validation stays in `field-validators.ts`; for the date, unreadable text maps to `''` with the same message rules (BR-06), replacing the `syncNative` path for dates only. The human accepts the three US-01 supersessions with this spec. **v0.2:** decided by ADR-0012 (amends ADR-0004): `@angular/aria` 22.3.0 + `@angular/cdk` 22.3.0; `<button>` combobox for select-only, `<input>` for searchable; `FormValueControl<string>`; dates through `transformedValue`; overlays outside the component root in jsdom. | US-04-Q-05 | **[Blocks HC1]** Date typed entry: format, accepted variants, how it maps to ISO, and what an incomplete or impossible date does. | Changes the US-01-AC-24 keyboard path (today: segments typed in the browser locale) and the R3-F01 tests; must keep the `badInput` semantics. | dd/mm/aaaa for every country, independent of browser locale; accepted: `d/m/yyyy` with `/`, `-` or `.` separators (1–2 digit day and month), or exactly 8 digits `ddmmyyyy`; 4-digit year only. Re-displayed as dd/mm/aaaa on leaving the field. Incomplete, impossible (31/04, 29/02 of a non-leap year) or 2-digit-year text → stored `''`, text kept, invalid with the existing message rules (no new validation message; a more specific "Ingresa una fecha válida (dd/mm/aaaa)." would be a validation-copy change and is not proposed). ### 11.1.1 Changes to existing tests for v0.3 (HC3 round 1; complete list)

Same rule as §11.1: each change follows a behaviour the human changed at HC3 (BR-07 exception
(a)–(e)) and keeps shown **and** stored assertions; nothing is deleted without a replacement.
Found with a search of `frontend/e2e/*.spec.ts`, `frontend/e2e/support/*.ts`,
`frontend/src/**/*.spec.ts` and `frontend/src/testing/*.ts` for the date required message, the
`fullName` message, `spinbutton`/`type: 'number'`/`badInput`, header focusability, chooser header
absence and the calendar position. Playwright `fill()` sets the whole value in one input event,
which the date mask handles like a paste (BR-18), so `fill('15/05/1990')` and `fill('5/5/1990')`
keep working.

**E2E**

| File | Test | Today | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| `us-01-data-form-co.spec.ts` | US-01-AC-02 / AC-10 / AC-18 "required date partly cleared" (R3-F01), 2 tests (`clearDateDigit`, `MESSAGE`) | "15/05/199" after leaving → "Ingresa tu fecha de nacimiento." | Same steps; the message is "Fecha no válida. Usa el formato dd/mm/aaaa." (BR-18); every other assertion unchanged. |
| `us-01-data-form-co.spec.ts` | US-01-AC-02 row `['Nombre completo', 'Al', …]` | "Ingresa tu nombre completo (entre 3 y 80 caracteres)." | "Ingresa tu nombre completo, solo letras (entre 3 y 80 caracteres)." (seed, §7.1). |
| `us-01-data-form-co.spec.ts` | US-01-AC-09 '"1e" typed key by key in "Modelo (año)"' | Native number: value `''`, `validity.badInput` true, stored `''`, yearRange message | Text box with the digits profile: "1e" shows "1" and stores "1" (`badInput` assertions removed: no native number control any more); "Continuar" shows "El modelo debe estar entre los últimos 20 años y el próximo año.", `aria-invalid`, stays on `/co/datos`. The `US-01-AC-09` ID stays; the title says the letter is not entered. |
| `us-01-data-form-co.spec.ts` | US-01-AC-09 '"abc" cannot even be typed into the number field' | Passes as is | Assertions unchanged; only the comment about the native number control is updated. |
| `us-01-data-form-co.spec.ts` | US-01-AC-24 keyboard completion, `tabTo('Tipo de documento', { max: 6 })` from the top | Header and indicator add no stop | Expected unchanged: the chip link and "Cambiar país" are two unlabelled stops before the first field, within `max: 6`; the test-engineer confirms. Typing "15/05/1990" key by key gives "15/05/1990" with the mask (AC-25 row). |
| `us-01-country-context.spec.ts` | US-01-AC-22 `expectEmptyStep1` | Loop over `getByRole('spinbutton')` | The year is now a textbox (covered by the textbox loop); replace the spinbutton loop with an assertion that the year text box (by label) has value `''`, so the check does not become vacuous. |
| `us-04-design-system.spec.ts` | US-04-AC-08 (es-CO and en-US) '"29/02/2001" … shows the required message' | `toHaveAccessibleDescription(/Ingresa tu fecha de nacimiento\./)` | `/Fecha no válida\. Usa el formato dd\/mm\/aaaa\./`; title updated; the rest unchanged. |
| `us-04-design-system.spec.ts` | US-04-AC-12 "1280 x 800, Elegir fecha: a popover anchored to the date field" | Accepts the popover above **or** below within 40 px | Below only, per AC-24 (or replaced by the AC-24 tests, which are stricter). The 768 × 1024 "Ciudad" test is unchanged (select panels are not in BR-17). |

**Component and unit**

| File | Test | Today | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| `src/testing/seed-fixtures.ts` | `fullName` (CO, CL), `documentNumber`, `plate` fixtures | Old seed | Mirror §7.1: `pattern` rule and new `errorMessage` for `fullName`; `maxLength` 10 / 12 / 6. |
| `src/app/shared/field-validators.spec.ts` | line ~181 `validateField(fullName, 'Al')` | Old message | New `fullName` message; plus the AC-26 pattern rows. |
| `quote-form-page.spec.ts` | US-01-AC-02 row `['Nombre completo', 'Al', …]` and the full-message assertion near line 306 | Old message | New message. The `toContain('Ingresa tu nombre completo')` substring checks stay valid. |
| `quote-form-page.spec.ts` | US-01-AC-01 "every field type renders its control … number (spinbutton)" | `Modelo (año)`: `{ tagName: 'INPUT', type: 'number' }` | `{ tagName: 'INPUT', type: 'text' }` with `inputmode="numeric"` and role textbox; title "number (text box, numeric)". |
| `quote-form-page.spec.ts` | US-01-AC-21 "what is typed is written as it changes" | Types "2015.5" in "Año", expects stored "2015.5" | Types "2015.5", expects shown and stored "2015" (the "." is not entered). The hydration test with stored "2015.5" is unchanged (US-04-Q-26: restored values are not filtered). |
| `quote-form-page.spec.ts` | US-01-AC-09 / AC-21 number "cannot parse" block (stubbed `validity.badInput`, 7 tests incl. Kilometraje "1e"/"2015e") | Stub sets `badInput` and value `''` | The stub no longer models a reachable state (text box, digits profile). Replace each with typing: "2015e" shows and stores "2015"; "1e" shows and stores "1"; the required-message and optional-message assertions move to an empty required year (requiredMessage ?? errorMessage) and to an out-of-range value, as ADR-0014 decides for the remaining `syncNative` path. The US-01-AC-09 IDs stay. |
| `quote-form-page.spec.ts` | US-01-AC-09 / AC-10 optional date "10/13/2026" (2 tests: errorMessage / "Revisa este campo.") | Shows the field's `errorMessage` or "Revisa este campo." | Both show "Fecha no válida. Usa el formato dd/mm/aaaa." (US-04-Q-24); other assertions unchanged. |
| `quote-form-page.spec.ts` | US-01-AC-02 / AC-10 / AC-18 "required date emptied after it was valid", rows "15/05/199" | "Ingresa tu fecha de nacimiento." | "Fecha no válida. Usa el formato dd/mm/aaaa." for the unreadable row; the cleared (`''`) row keeps "Ingresa tu fecha de nacimiento.". |
| `src/app/shared/date-field.spec.ts` | US-04-AC-08 rows 29/02/2001, 31/04/1990, 15/05/199, 15/05/90 (`REQUIRED`), the "unreadable text is the former badInput" test and the optional "Fecha de revisión" test | Required / field message | "Fecha no válida. Usa el formato dd/mm/aaaa."; stored `''` and visible text unchanged. |
| `src/app/shared/date-field.spec.ts` | US-04-AC-08 "no input mask: typing '15' leaves '15'" | Asserts no `/` inserted | Replaced by the AC-25 mask rows ("150" → "15/0"); the test of "15" alone may stay with a true title. |
| `src/app/shared/wizard-chrome.spec.ts` | US-04-AC-13 "neither the indicator nor the header contains a focusable element or a heading" | Header: 0 focusable | Indicator: 0; header: exactly 1 focusable element, the chip link (AC-13 v0.3, AC-28); headings 0. |
| `src/app/shared/wizard-chrome.spec.ts` | US-04-AC-13 "the Tab order of step 3 is unchanged … first stop is 'Editar mis datos'" | First stop "Editar mis datos" | First stops: chip link, "Volver a planes", then "Editar mis datos" (AC-28). |
| `country-chooser-page.spec.ts` | US-04-AC-03 "the chooser is not a wizard page: no wizard header and no step indicator" | `header, [role="banner"]` is null | A header with "Cotizador de seguro de auto" and no link, no chip and no `data-country-accent`; no step indicator (AC-29). |
| `contrast.spec.ts`, `design-guards.spec.ts` | Read `contrast-pairs.json` and `tokens.css` | — | Expected unchanged in code; the data changes (new rows per gradient stop). New AC-27 guard added. |

Not affected (checked): `quote-form-page.spec.ts` US-01-AC-17 link lists on `/`, `/ar/datos` and
the country-error state (`querySelectorAll('a')`): the chooser header has no link and no back link
or chip link renders without a resolved country (BR-21); `us-01-country-context.spec.ts` link
queries run on pages without the chip; the US-02-AC-16 / US-03-AC-16 keyboard tests Tab forward from
the focused `h1`, after the new stops.

## US-04 spec v0.3 (HC3 round 1) is written

I revised two files. Nothing else was touched, and nothing was committed.
- `/Users/cristiansabogal/Proyectos/multicountry-car-insurance/specs/US-04/spec.md`, now **v0.3**. Status stays `Approved` because the human directed these changes at HC3. The header and the Review log say the concrete values are the main session's recommendation, which the human reviews in this round's HC3 QA.
- `/Users/cristiansabogal/Proyectos/multicountry-car-insurance/specs/US-04/tasks.md`: Current step is HC3 round 1 changes. Next action is the test-engineer on T-29 and T-30. I added tasks T-27..T-40 and two Gate history rows.

**Counts:** 21 BR (+5), 29 AC (0 original / 29 derived; +6), 27 Q (+5). Q-23..Q-27 are open and none blocks.

## IDs added
- **Business rules:**
  - BR-17: compact calendar, directly below the date field, never over the header.
  - BR-18: date mask, paste handling and the invalid-date message.
  - BR-19: input profiles, `maxlength`, number fields become `type="text" inputmode="numeric"`, and the seed content changes.
  - BR-20: `--gradient-page` background on every page, plus the richer chooser. D4 and D6 share this one BR to keep BR-17..21.
  - BR-21: back links, chip link, change of country, header not clipped.
- **Acceptance criteria:** AC-24 calendar, AC-25 typed date, AC-26 profiles and seed, AC-27 background, AC-28 back navigation, AC-29 chooser.
- **Gaps, each with a proposed default:**
  - Q-23: mask details (what a typed separator does, Backspace over `/`).
  - Q-24: the invalid-date message also applies to optional date fields.
  - Q-25: chooser order is h1, lead, country links, then "Cómo funciona".
  - Q-26: restored values are not filtered; the plate is stored in upper case.
  - Q-27: the `fullName` seed pattern uses the Latin-1 class `^[A-Za-zÀ-ÖØ-öø-ÿ][A-Za-zÀ-ÖØ-öø-ÿ '.-]*$`. The validator has no `u` flag, so `\p{L}` cannot be used. This class includes the brief's explicit Spanish class.
- **Tasks:** T-27..T-40. T-40 is a spec-writer follow-up: a US-01 Review log row and an update to `specs/US-01/seed-fields.md`.

**Amended (replaced text struck, not deleted):**
- §1 and §2, the glossary.
- BR-06, BR-07 (explicit HC3 exception list (a)–(e); under `backend/`, only `backend/src/seed/form-fields.ts` may change), BR-13 (two new Tab stops at the top of each step).
- AC-02 note, AC-08 (four error cells, the optional-date message, the note), AC-09 note, AC-11 (Strapi scenario exception), AC-12, AC-13, AC-22 note.
- v0.3 notes on Q-05, Q-07 and Q-17. I did not touch any *Human answer* cell.
- §7.1 seed table, §7.2 input-profile map and table, §8, §8.1, §9, §10, §11 rows for AC-24..29, a new §11.1.1, and the §13 rows for the human's request and v0.3.

## New copy strings (code-owned, §8.1)
- "Fecha no válida. Usa el formato dd/mm/aaaa."
- "Cambiar país" (step 1 back link to `/`; also the optional visible hint on the chip)
- "Volver a tus datos" (step 2 back link)
- "Volver a planes" (step 3 back link)
- "Cambiar país (actual: {país})", the chip link's accessible name, e.g. "Cambiar país (actual: Colombia)"
- "Cotiza el seguro de tu auto en pocos minutos. Elige el país donde está matriculado tu vehículo para ver los planes y precios disponibles."
- "Cómo funciona"
- "Cuéntanos sobre ti y tu vehículo." / "Compara coberturas y precios." / "Revisa, acepta los términos y paga." These go with the reused step names "Tus datos", "Plan" and "Resumen y pago".

The new Strapi seed text, which is not code-owned, is "Ingresa tu nombre completo, solo letras (entre 3 y 80 caracteres)."

## Existing tests that must change (full detail in spec §11.1.1)
**E2E**
- `frontend/e2e/us-01-data-form-co.spec.ts`:
  - The two "required date partly cleared" tests (R3-F01) now expect "Fecha no válida…".
  - The `'Nombre completo', 'Al'` row expects the new seed message.
  - The US-01-AC-09 `"1e"` test: the year box now shows and stores "1", the `badInput` assertions go, and the yearRange message stays.
  - The `"abc"` test: only a comment changes.
- `frontend/e2e/us-01-country-context.spec.ts`: the `expectEmptyStep1` spinbutton loop would become vacuous. It needs an explicit check that the year text box is `''`.
- `frontend/e2e/us-04-design-system.spec.ts`:
  - AC-08 `"29/02/2001"` (both locales): expected message becomes "Fecha no válida…".
  - AC-12 1280 date popover: below only, which is stricter than today's "above or below".

**Component and unit**
- `frontend/src/testing/seed-fixtures.ts`: mirror the new seed.
- `frontend/src/app/shared/field-validators.spec.ts`: the `'Al'` message.
- `frontend/src/app/features/quote-form/quote-form-page.spec.ts`:
  - The `fullName` message row and the full-message assertion near line 306.
  - US-01-AC-01: number control becomes `type: 'text'` with `inputmode="numeric"`.
  - US-01-AC-21: typing "2015.5" now shows and stores "2015".
  - The US-01-AC-09 block of 7 tests that stub `badInput` must be replaced by real typing.
  - The two optional-date "10/13/2026" tests and the "15/05/199" row of the R3-F01 tests expect the new message.
- `frontend/src/app/shared/date-field.spec.ts`: the four `REQUIRED` rows, the "former badInput" test and the optional-date test expect the new message. The "no input mask" test has a false title once the mask exists.
- `frontend/src/app/shared/wizard-chrome.spec.ts`: the header now has exactly one focusable element (the chip link). On step 3 the first Tab stops become the chip, "Volver a planes", then "Editar mis datos".
- `frontend/src/app/features/country/country-chooser-page.spec.ts`: "no wizard header" becomes "a header with the product name, no link, no chip, no indicator".

**Checked and not affected:** the US-01-AC-17 link lists (no chip or back link renders without a resolved country); the US-02-AC-16 and US-03-AC-16 keyboard tests (they Tab forward from the focused h1); US-01-AC-24 `tabTo(max: 6)`, which tolerates the two new stops at the top (the test-engineer should confirm).

**One note for the tests:** Playwright `fill()` sets the whole value in one input event, and the mask must handle that like a paste. Otherwise `fill('5/5/1990')` breaks. ADR-0014 needs to guarantee this.

## Gaps that block HC1
None. The spec stays Approved, and Q-23..Q-27 carry defaults for the HC3 QA.

## ADRs needed
- **ADR-0014** "Input profiles, typed-date mask and anchored calendar; page background", which amends ADR-0012 and ADR-0010. §10 lists what it must decide, including what remains of the `syncNative`/`badInput` path for number fields, which the replacement of the US-01-AC-09 tests depends on. It must be Accepted by the human before implementation (T-31..T-35).
